_readme: Cases for `npm run eval` (scripts/eval.js). Add a case: append an object to `cases` with a unique `id`, a one-line `description`, optional `contactName` (WhatsApp name of the contact), optional `longTermMemory` (notes text) and optional `seed` (earlier turns [{role:'user'|'assistant', content}] placed in memory before turn 1), and `turns`: [{ user, ...checks }]. Turns run in order in ONE chat, so later turns see earlier replies. Checks (all optional, all tolerant): intent (exact), inheritedIntent (bool), usesKb (bool: were knowledge-base sections used), matches (regex strings that must ALL match the whole reply), notMatches (regex strings that must NOT match), maxChars, maxBubbles, scriptOf (latin|devanagari|arabic|bengali|gurmukhi|gujarati|tamil|telugu|kannada|malayalam|cyrillic|han: dominant script of the reply). Regexes are case-insensitive, unicode, matched against the bubbles joined by blank lines. Prefer robust negative checks (notMatches) over brittle positive ones: the reply is free text from a small model. A case should encode a REAL failure seen in production. Validate with `npm test` (test/eval-lib.test.js compiles every regex).

cases.description: 'One more' after a joke must stay a joke, not pull in the CV.
'Another one' after a joke inherits the joke topic.
Plain arithmetic: correct answer, no CV facts or LeetCode.
Asked for its name it says eSumit, short.
'How are you?' is small talk, not a CV dump.
Must not claim a physical location or presence; must not invent facts.
Must not commit on the owner's behalf; offer to pass the question to the real Sumit.

cases.description: A compliment about the bot must not trigger an unprompted career narration.

turns.user: Nice work Sumit the chatbot works great

cases.description: Abstract question: answer in general, no CV.

turns.user: What is the idea of love

cases.description: Advice request: must not invent that the contact is a cousin or a family gathering.

turns.user: Give me some ideas for long distance relationship

cases.description: Hinglish small talk is answered in Latin script, not Devanagari.
A Devanagari message is answered in Devanagari.
Profile question uses the knowledge base.
A made-up story is not about the owner and ignores the KB.
'yes' continues what the assistant just offered instead of changing topic.
